confidence: high that the vocabulary overlaps; medium that the overlap produces a wrong route
label: The renamed surface still owns the runtime's own name in routing vocabulary: v4.0.0.13 renamed sk-code-opencode to sk-code-skilled because 'the code check no longer shares a name with the OpenCode runtime', but sk-code-skilled still scores the bare token 'opencode' plus 'opencode system code', 'opencode system code workflow' and 'opencode typescript verification', while the sibling hub cli-external-orchestration claims bare 'opencode' at weight 4 through its cli-opencode signal; because sk-code declares defaultMode null and outcomes.single routes a surface alone when no workflow mode scores, 'opencode system code' lands on the read-only sk-code-skilled surface and plain 'opencode' is contested by two hub identities.

confidence: high that the gate reads no router; high that the three probes are absent from it
label: The fleet gate added at v4.0.0.15 (ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs) validates root metadata for all 14 skill roots and passes, but it reads no hub-router.json and no mode-registry.json, so a hub can have a conforming root and a broken routing pair; extend the same gate with three assertions that all pass today for sk-code (5 modes), sk-design (3) and sk-doc (15): registry workflowMode set equals routerSignals key set, every packet names an existing folder, and every quality checklist path resolves.

Routing identity holds in all three hubs: registry mode set equals router signal set (sk-code 5, sk-design 3, sk-doc 15), with zero registry-only modes, zero signal-only modes, zero missing packet folders and zero missing quality-checklist files.
No orphan routing vocabulary: sk-code 15 declared classes (14 referenced + hub-identity in discoveryClasses), sk-design 3/3, sk-doc 17/17, and zero referenced-but-undeclared classes in any hub.
The v4.0.0.15 root-metadata contract is satisfied by all four hubs: ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs reports checked=14 passed=14 failed=0, exit 0.

The parent-hub schema doc was corrected in the same release that added sk-code-frontend (v4.0.2.0, version 1.2.10.0, three surfaces and an updated tieBreak), so the earlier 'four packets' wording was accurate when written rather than stale.
sk-prompt keeps its v4.0.2.0 rename of cli-hermes to cli-deepseek-harness and carries no DEPTH framework reference outside archived benchmark stderr blobs.
